sample_unit: infants <32 weeks GA or <1500 g birth weight

links.outcome: Failed extubation rate (reintubation <5 days) before vs after standardization and EMR calculator
links.effect: Failed extubations fell from 10.3% to 2.3%, with special cause variation after both PDSA cycles; ventilator days fell 10.8 to 7.0. Uncontrolled pre-post design.
links.quote: We observed a reduction in failed extubations from 10.3% to 2.3%, with special cause variation noted after both plan-do-study-act cycle #1 and #2.

links.outcome: Balancing measures: days on mechanical ventilation and infants intubated <3 days
links.effect: Average infants intubated <3 days increased (60.2%-73.6%) while average ventilator days decreased (10.8-7.0).
links.quote: Additionally, the average number of infants intubated <3 days increased (60.2%-73.6%), whereas average ventilator days decreased (10.8-7.0).

unlisted_practices: Standardizing postextubation respiratory support alongside a predictive decision support tool
Quality improvement PDSA cycles with statistical process control charts to evaluate AI-enabled clinical practice change

screen.reason: The study evaluates a quality improvement real-world clinical deployment of an EMR-integrated real-time extubation predictive calculator alongside clinical standardization to reduce extubation failure in neonates.
